# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, remove an English sentence the Korean does not support, or fix a character's name or pronoun as described below.

## Names and pronouns

The packet lists the profiled characters named in this chapter with their gender, and any required name corrections.

- Use the glossary or character-card English for every name. Apply each required name correction everywhere it occurs.
- Korean usually omits pronouns. When a card gives `female` or `male` and the English uses the other pronoun for that character, fix the pronoun. Leave pronouns alone for a character whose gender is `unknown`.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Never write a footnote whose job is to identify or describe a story character, creature, pet, group, place, item, or plot event. The story introduces its own cast; a note must not say who someone is, what they did, or what a name refers to inside the story. This holds even when the glossary or a character card explains the name: those are reference for you, not footnote material.

When a story name coincides with a real person, brand, or work (Magic Johnson, Mimi), the name is the story's. Do not footnote the real one unless the Korean source itself makes that reference.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not repeat a panel. A notice the mastered chapter already shows more than once stays repeated that many times, and no more. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

—Kyaaaah!

“Fire Wall!”

“Lightning Spear!”

*Fwoooosh.*

Slowly. Carefully.

We had to win while keeping our losses to a minimum.

Besides…

The bastard who had yet to show himself.

The Prophet.

Until we took them down, neither this battle nor the war would end.

*Thud. Thud. Thuuum.*

Heavenly Strike.

“Fire!”

“Fire Wall!”

“Lightning Spear!”

*Fwoooosh.*

The Prophet.

*This fight… is only just beginning.*

And at that moment, just as I muttered those words deep in my heart—

*Thud. Thud. Thuuum.*

An immense magical power surged from far away, making the desert tremble.

# Chapter 803

Human beings possess almost limitless potential.

With minds more capable than those of any other living thing on Earth, they built systems of their own and developed civilization.

From the primitive prehistoric age to the present, what humans had achieved was dazzling—especially the history and culture they had built over the past several thousand years.

Progress, progress, and more progress.

Humans never stopped discovering new things. With each discovery, they moved forward.

Until gunfire filled battlefields where swords and spears had once clashed. Until car horns replaced the whinny of horses on streets lit by neon signs.

Until they crossed five seas and six continents and finally ventured into space.

*“Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.”*

On the day that grand plan, named after an ancient sun god, succeeded, what did the god watching from somewhere think? A human had set foot on the moon for the first time and called that historic moment “one small step, one giant leap for mankind.”

No one could know the will of God. But an old man with the rather long name Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Ali was certain.

God must have been enraged.

Otherwise, He would not have unleashed a great flood called the Great Cataclysm.

Sending the great Prophet down to this land and commanding him to punish them surely meant that he was to punish humanity’s arrogance on God’s behalf.

“Do you not think so too, sinful infidel?”

“…!”

The middle-aged man trembled at the old man’s calm voice.

Drenched in blood, he stood amid his many subordinates. Only moments ago, they had been alive and breathing. Now they lay strewn across the ground.

He had nothing left but the sword in his hand and the mana boiling through his body, his fighting spirit still undiminished.

“Atone through death. Like those who went before you.”

“Go… fuck yourself!”

With a shout like a scream, the middle-aged man drew on every ounce of his strength and charged the old fanatic.

*Whoooosh!*

A strike that would likely be his last.

His sword flew faster than ever before, its blade blazing with aura.

*Shhk!*

A flash came out of nowhere, cleaving both the aura-wreathed sword and its wielder in two.

*Splatter!*

Blood gushed like a fountain.

As the headless corpse crumpled, something glinting fell at the old man’s feet.

A necklace. It was a necklace.

The old man stared at the crucifix necklace half-buried in the hot sand, then spoke.

“Any survivors?”

“None. That infidel was the last.”

The young man who had cut down the middle-aged A-rank Hunter as easily as breathing continued, “Amir, there are more infidels not far from here. If you let me go…”

“Their main force will have heard from them over the radio this time. We’ve dealt with them easily so far, but it won’t be that simple from now on.”

“No matter how strong the infidels’ forces are, we can defeat them!”

“You’re right, Hamid, son of Hassan. But have you forgotten what the Prophet said?”

Hamid flinched at the old man’s piercing gaze. A moment later, he realized what Amir meant, and his eyes widened.

“What the Prophet said… Could it be?”

“Yes. The time has finally come. The time promised by the Prophet and almighty Allah is upon us.”

“…!”

Surprise turned to joy. Joy to fervor.

The old man smiled as he watched Hamid’s expression change. Then he looked over the warriors of God surrounding them and murmured, “Inshallah. The Prophet will lead us to the promised land!”

“Inshallah!”

“Allah hu akbar!”

Their voices rose together in a mighty shout. The countless fanatics who had lain dormant deep in the desert for decades began their advance.

Toward the promised land they had awaited for so long.

Toward the place overflowing with God’s grace.

*Rumble, rumble, rumble!*

A vast cloud of sand swept across the desert.

* * *

If this world were a chessboard, what would my role be?

A pawn that could only move forward?

A knight that could go farther than a pawn?

A bishop crossing the board diagonally?

Maybe a rook moving in straight lines, a queen with the combined reach of a bishop and a rook, or the king—ironically, the most important piece and yet weaker than the queen.

Honestly, I didn’t know.

Even now, as the Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation, even with everyone in the world knowing who I was, I still didn’t know exactly where I stood.

But one thing I could say for sure.

If that chessboard was a battlefield rather than the world, I could dominate it.

I could push forward like a pawn, leap over my enemies’ heads like a knight, then range across the board like a bishop, rook, or queen and swallow everything in my path.

Just like right now.

*Baaang!*

Flesh and bone burst apart before the spearhead even touched them. A Troll with its upper half blown away toppled like a rotten log, and someone shouted behind me.

“Damn it! How many times do I have to tell you? Kill them like that and I can barely use them as undead!”

Instead of answering, I twisted my body.

*Whoom. Boom!*

Three flails flying in from different directions tangled together.

—Kwo?

The ogres blinked stupidly, a beat too late to understand what had happened.

White Flame’s spearhead had already swept past their necks.

*Shhk!*

Three heads flew free of their massive bodies.

I sprang off an ogre’s lifeless corpse and plunged toward the monsters packed around me.

Fire Dragon Divine Spear, Form Two.

Heavenly Strike.

*Krrrunch!*

Blood sprayed. Flesh split.

*Ding. Ding, ding.*

System alerts rang in my ears without pause as I leaped into the thick cloud of dust.

*Open Inventory.*

One weapon stored, another summoned at the same instant.

*Pop.*

White Flame vanished from my hand like an illusion. In its place, two short daggers settled firmly into my hands.

In a fight at this close range, they were faster and more efficient than any divine weapon.

I’d watched someone wield a dagger like this up close. With a single blade, he had earned the name Slaughter Saint.

*And I watched him do it from right beside him.*

For one brief moment, I steadied my breathing.

I calmed the internal energy pounding as though it would burst out of me. Light on my toes. Shoulders loose.

Remembering the Slaughter Saint’s advice, I copied the movements I’d seen him perform right in front of me dozens of times.

Then I took a step.

*Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step.*

*Swish.*

The wind that had always struck me head-on now slipped gently past.

I felt as though I were floating through the air in zero gravity.

Of course, I couldn’t claim I’d perfectly copied the Slaughter Saint’s personal martial art just by doing this much. But for dealing with these bastards right now, this much was enough.

*Shhk, shhk, shhk!*

The sound of slicing reached my ears only after flesh and bone had been cut.

Sound wasn’t slow.

I was fast enough to leave it behind. So were the daggers in my hands.

*Thud, thud, thud!*

I slipped among the monsters like mist, my daggers stabbing and slashing in flashes. Dozens fell, spraying blood.

No—they fell and rose again at the same moment.

—In the king’s name, I command you: answer the call.

*Whoooooosh.*

A voice seemed to ring inside my head rather than reach my ears, and a chilling cold swept across the battlefield.

It raised the monsters that had fallen moments ago and those falling even now.

—Krr. Grrrk.

Slow, rasping cries.

An eerie light glimmered deep in their eyes.

Reborn as new beings at the edge of death, the undead army obeyed their king’s command. Without hesitation, they charged the monsters pouring in from every direction.

—Kraaaaaa!

—Grr. Uh. Uh. Uh!

*Thud. Kraaang!*

The cries of living and undead monsters tangled together. Weapons swung hard into bodies on both sides.

But the living monsters felt pain. The undead had forgotten it when they died.

—Graaah.

*Crunch! Splatter!*

Outnumbered? It didn’t matter.

Even when weapons took their limbs or pierced their chests, they kept moving to the very end.

The Skeleton King had given them only one goal: before the magical power he had bestowed on them ran out, before they died a second death, they were to create another soldier.

*Crack!*

—Kyaaaah!

A monster screamed as its throat was torn out.

The undead that had done it, already missing an arm and a leg, was ripped to shreds by enraged monsters. That didn’t matter either.

Thanks to that, I—

No, we—had bought a little more time.

“Fire!”

“Fire Wall!”

“Lightning Spear!”

*Fwoooosh.*

Countless bolts of lightning and tongues of flame streaked through the air.

Behind the enormous transport vehicle blocking the way like a barricade, the monsters packed in so tightly there wasn’t a gap—like the first day of an E-Mart Black Friday sale—had no choice but to take the sudden barrage of attacks head-on.

*Crackle. KRAAAASH!*

—Kraaaaaa!

—Kgh! Grrrk!

Screams filled the air.

Lightning seared scales and flesh. Flames slipped through the gaps and burned bone and organs.

Many of the hundreds of monsters writhing in pain unlike anything they had ever felt even swung their weapons at their own allies.

—Kwoooooo!

Seized by their own savage instincts, the monsters charged one another.

But I didn’t let my guard down for a second.

“Hold formation! Don’t move a single step!”

I drove internal energy into the command. The Hunters who had begun advancing, swept up in the heat of battle and the thrill of gaining the upper hand, stopped in their tracks.

Battle was flow. Battle was momentum.

But there was a time to ride that momentum.

Against a force of well over ten thousand, taking out a mere thousand monsters wouldn’t win us the battle all at once.

Slowly. Carefully.

We had to win while keeping our losses to a minimum.

Besides…

*I still can’t see him.*

The bastard who had yet to show himself.

The Prophet.

And the S-rank monsters waiting for their moment among that sea of beasts—or somewhere in the sky above.

Until we took them down, neither this battle nor the war would end.

*This fight… is only just beginning.*

And at that moment, just as I muttered those words deep in my heart—

*Thud. Thud. Thuuum.*

An immense magical power surged from far away, making the desert tremble.
